title: Impact of School Finance Reform on Math Test Scores

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Difference-in-Differences (DID) with two-way (school and period) fixed effects.
- Why: We observe treated and control schools before and after a statewide school finance reform. DID compares the change in outcomes for treated schools to the contemporaneous change for control schools, netting out time-invariant school characteristics and common time shocks.
- Parameter of interest: The coefficient on treated × post (the average treatment effect on the treated).
- Key assumptions:
  - Parallel trends: In the absence of reform, treated and control schools would have experienced similar trends in math scores.
  - No spillovers: Treatment of one school does not affect outcomes in control schools.
  - Stable composition and measurement over time (SUTVA): No differential changes in who is tested or how tests are measured across groups except via the reform.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Complete, self-contained R code

# 1) Setup ---------------------------------------------------------------------
pkgs <- c("fixest", "sandwich", "lmtest", "readr", "dplyr")
to_install <- pkgs[!sapply(pkgs, requireNamespace, quietly = TRUE)]
if (length(to_install) > 0) install.packages(to_install, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")

library(fixest)
library(sandwich)
library(lmtest)
library(readr)
library(dplyr)

# 2) Load data -----------------------------------------------------------------
dat <- readr::read_csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s35_data.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

# Coerce types and create FE-friendly variables
dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(
    unit_id     = as.integer(unit_id),
    period_num  = as.integer(period),
    treated     = as.integer(treated),
    post        = as.integer(post),
    treat_x_post = as.integer(treat_x_post),
    unit_id_f   = factor(unit_id),
    period_f    = factor(period_num)
  )

# Basic info
n_units   <- dplyr::n_distinct(dat$unit_id)
n_periods <- dplyr::n_distinct(dat$period_num)
cat("Data loaded. Schools (units):", n_units, "| Periods:", n_periods, "\n")

# Sanity checks on support
tab <- dat %>% count(treated, post)
cat("Cell counts by treated x post:\n")
print(tab)

# 3) Baseline DID (pooled OLS) with unit-clustered SE --------------------------
m_ols <- lm(y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post, data = dat)
V_ols <- sandwich::vcovCL(m_ols, cluster = dat$unit_id)  # cluster by school
co_ols <- lmtest::coeftest(m_ols, vcov = V_ols)

beta_ols <- co_ols["treat_x_post", "Estimate"]
se_ols   <- co_ols["treat_x_post", "Std. Error"]
p_ols    <- co_ols["treat_x_post", "Pr(>|t|)"]
ci_ols   <- beta_ols + c(-1, 1) * 1.96 * se_ols

cat("\nBaseline DID (OLS, unit-clustered SE):\n")
cat("  beta_DID =", round(beta_ols, 4),
    "| SE =", round(se_ols, 4),
    "| 95% CI = [", round(ci_ols[1], 4), ",", round(ci_ols[2], 4), "]",
    "| p =", signif(p_ols, 3), "\n")

# 4) Two-way fixed effects DID (school and period FE), clustered by unit -------
m_twfe <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id_f + period_f, data = dat, cluster = ~ unit_id_f)

beta_twfe <- coef(m_twfe)["treat_x_post"]
se_twfe   <- sqrt(vcov(m_twfe)["treat_x_post", "treat_x_post"])
p_twfe    <- summary(m_twfe)$coeftable["treat_x_post", "Pr(>|t|)"]
ci_twfe   <- beta_twfe + c(-1, 1) * 1.96 * se_twfe

cat("\nTwo-way FE DID (unit & period FE, clustered by unit):\n")
cat("  beta_DID =", round(beta_twfe, 4),
    "| SE =", round(se_twfe, 4),
    "| 95% CI = [", round(ci_twfe[1], 4), ",", round(ci_twfe[2], 4), "]",
    "| p =", signif(p_twfe, 3), "\n")

# 5) Robustness: Two-way clustered SE (unit and period) ------------------------
m_twfe_2c <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id_f + period_f, data = dat, cluster = ~ unit_id_f + period_f)

beta_twfe_2c <- coef(m_twfe_2c)["treat_x_post"]
se_twfe_2c   <- sqrt(vcov(m_twfe_2c)["treat_x_post", "treat_x_post"])
p_twfe_2c    <- summary(m_twfe_2c)$coeftable["treat_x_post", "Pr(>|t|)"]
ci_twfe_2c   <- beta_twfe_2c + c(-1, 1) * 1.96 * se_twfe_2c

cat("\nTwo-way FE DID with two-way clustered SE (unit & period):\n")
cat("  beta_DID =", round(beta_twfe_2c, 4),
    "| SE =", round(se_twfe_2c, 4),
    "| 95% CI = [", round(ci_twfe_2c[1], 4), ",", round(ci_twfe_2c[2], 4), "]",
    | "p =", signif(p_twfe_2c, 3), "\n")

# 6) Robustness: Event-study style pre-trend test ------------------------------
# Define last pre-reform period and first post, if available
if (any(dat$post == 0) && any(dat$post == 1)) {
  last_pre   <- max(dat$period_num[dat$post == 0])
  first_post <- min(dat$period_num[dat$post == 1])

  # Event-study with ref = last pre; includes unit FE and period FE
  m_es <- feols(y ~ i(period_num, treated, ref = last_pre) | unit_id_f + period_num,
                data = dat, cluster = ~ unit_id_f)

  coefs_names <- names(coef(m_es))
  # Coefficients are named like "period_num::k#treated"
  pre_names <- grep("^period_num::[0-9]+#treated$", coefs_names, value = TRUE)
  pre_periods <- as.integer(sub("^period_num::([0-9]+)#treated$", "\\1", pre_names))
  pre_to_test <- pre_names[pre_periods < last_pre]

  if (length(pre_to_test) >= 1) {
    constraints <- paste0(pre_to_test, " = 0")
    w <- wald(m_es, constraints = constraints)
    cat("\nEvent-study pre-trend joint test (H0: all pre-period treated-time coeffs = 0):\n")
    cat("  F-stat =", round(w$stat, 3), "| p-value =", signif(w$p.value, 3), "\n")
  } else {
    cat("\nEvent-study pre-trend test: not enough distinct pre-periods to test.\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("\nEvent-study pre-trend test: data lack clear pre and post periods.\n")
}

# 7) Final numerical result printout -------------------------------------------
cat("\nPrimary estimate (Two-way FE DID, clustered by unit):\n")
cat("  Effect of finance reform on math scores (SD units):",
    round(beta_twfe, 4), "\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Positive. School finance reforms typically increase funding in historically under-resourced districts, improving inputs (class size, teacher quality, instructional materials) and leading to higher test scores.
- Magnitude: About 0.05–0.15 standard deviations in math scores in the post-reform periods for treated schools, with effects potentially growing over time. The DID coefficient should be within this range if the reform meaningfully altered resources and if there is adequate time for effects to materialize.
- Diagnostics: We expect no significant pre-trend differences (joint pre-period coefficients near zero). Robustness using two-way clustering should not overturn significance if the effect is sizable.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: We compare changes in math test scores over time between schools affected by the reform and those that were not.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The reform led to a decrease in math test scores.
